narration.en: In a formula, the central atom is written first, followed by the ligands in alphabetical order; the whole coordination entity is enclosed in square brackets, and polyatomic ligands in parentheses. The charge of a complex ion is shown outside the bracket as a superscript, and the counter ion is written like any other ion: the cation first.
narration.kn: ಸೂತ್ರದಲ್ಲಿ ಕೇಂದ್ರ ಪರಮಾಣು ಮೊದಲು, ನಂತರ ಲಿಗ್ಯಾಂಡ್‌ಗಳು ವರ್ಣಾನುಕ್ರಮದಲ್ಲಿ; ಸಂಪೂರ್ಣ ಸಮನ್ವಯ ಘಟಕ ಚೌಕ ಕಂಸದಲ್ಲಿ.

body.en: Name the cation first, then the anion. Within the complex, name the ligands in alphabetical order before the metal. Prefixes di-, tri-, tetra- count simple ligands; bis-, tris-, tetrakis- are used for ligands whose names already contain a number, such as (ethane-1,2-diamine). Anionic ligands end in -o: chlorido, cyanido, hydroxido, oxalato. Neutral ligands keep their names except aqua (H₂O), ammine (NH₃), carbonyl (CO) and nitrosyl (NO). Give the oxidation state of the metal in Roman numerals. If the complex is an anion, the metal name ends in -ate, using Latin roots for some: ferrate (Fe), cuprate (Cu), argentate (Ag), aurate (Au), plumbate (Pb), stannate (Sn).
body.kn: ಮೊದಲು ಧನ ಅಯಾನು, ನಂತರ ಋಣ ಅಯಾನು. ಲಿಗ್ಯಾಂಡ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು ವರ್ಣಾನುಕ್ರಮದಲ್ಲಿ ಹೆಸರಿಸಿ, ನಂತರ ಲೋಹ ಮತ್ತು ರೋಮನ್ ಅಂಕಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಆಕ್ಸಿಡೀಕರಣ ಸ್ಥಿತಿ. ಋಣ ಸಂಕೀರ್ಣದಲ್ಲಿ ಲೋಹದ ಹೆಸರು -ate ನಲ್ಲಿ ಕೊನೆಗೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತದೆ.

steps.en: (a) Cation complex: x − 1 = +2 → Co(III). Ligands alphabetically: ammine, chlorido.
(b) Anion complex [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻: x − 6 = −3 → Fe(III); anion, so "ferrate".

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Name (a) [Co(NH₃)₅Cl]Cl₂ and (b) K₃[Fe(CN)₆].

problem.en: Write the formula of potassium tetrahydroxidozincate(II).

steps.en: Anionic complex of Zn(II) with four OH⁻: charge = +2 − 4 = −2, so [Zn(OH)₄]²⁻.
Two K⁺ balance the charge: K₂[Zn(OH)₄].

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Write the formula of potassium tetrahydroxidozincate(II).

body.en: Look at the charge on the bracket. Cationic or neutral complex: the plain metal name (cobalt, platinum). Anionic complex: -ate, with the Latin root for Fe, Cu, Ag, Au, Pb and Sn.
